    Wednesday 7 October 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    The share column ships flat at the room's median - 10 names, 1 of them short, their order an unshipped shadow (R81) - and the option column ships the room's own G_OPTION median on 10 legs (R79; the owner's ten a day - 0 DESK-FILLED, 6 R4-OVERFLOW (owner, 2026-10-06) at half stake), led by AMZN 2026-10-16 $260C at 55.0; watchdog sits suspended on a congressional feed that still serves no record count, and the board sat after the open

    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any). OVERNIGHT: Asia's last bars are stale and mostly up (Nikkei 225 +1.05%, Hang Seng +1.00%, KOSPI -0.89%), Europe closed down (DAX -1.35%, Euro Stoxx 50 -1.47%; -1.20% avg over 3) and the US futures read down (-0.35% avg over 2), so Asia and the futures disagree - the shape that most often retraces. Expected shape: a morning move that retraces and then reclaims; the gap reads already show it on several names (MU, SMCI and VST opened down and traded back through), and this board sat after the open, so the court scores only the tape from the freeze to the close, with SPY -0.2 and QQQ -0.3 on the day at the freeze. REGIME: risk-on: SPY +2.0% 5d, VIX 15.1 falling - but the freeze tape is softer, with IWM -1.14 on the day and the US 10-year yield 5.29 and the dollar index 102.25 both up; the cycle composite projects +2.07% over the next 10 trading days, a forecast, not a fact. CONVICTION: the option column is ONE bet - ten long calls on AI-infrastructure, semiconductor and power beta, all on the 2026-10-16 expiry - and spreading it over ten tickers is a variance instrument that does not change that bet's mean; its best expression, AMZN (REQMOVE 0.378), already carries the column's top grade. The share column leans defensive - health care and staples longs with three megacap software names and one pharma short (BMY) - and ships flat at 1.0 per line (R81). ALLOCATION: a name the room graded in both columns ships where the book's total room median is higher (AMZN, HPE, VST and MU to options; CVS, BMY and MSFT to shares), and the tie at 50.0 for the last share slot (AVGO, ADBE, MCK) is broken by the room's share mean, which seats MCK.

    WHAT KILLS IT: the option column dies together on a tech-led reversal - closes below 248.54 on AMZN, 65.92 on HPE and 40.65 on SMCI kill its three top legs - while each share line dies on its own kill close, the BMY short on a close above 62.25. PYRAMID: the leader is blackswan, and its read carries no extra weight (R33). It diverges from the room most on MU, filing a contract grade of 72 against the room's 51.0 (72-51.0 = 21.0) and a share grade of 37 against 51.5 - it buys convexity on the high-sigma names and holds the calm names as shares. CALIBRATION: no FILED seat's grade_return_corr is above timekeeper's 0.032, so weighting cannot separate the room and every shipped line files at the gate's median (R78, R79). The model disagrees sharply with three shipped lines - COST -3.8772, HPE -3.7182, CEG -3.9234 - and its CTVA 247.0286 is an artefact of the -81.37 break; it authors no departure. ROSTER (served labels only, R110): 13 FILED seats in each column; watchdog SUSPENDED; domestic_desk NON-FILING; decoder SHADOW (R27) and NON-FILING in the R92 block. R92: PLTR files SERVED 50.0 / GATE 51.0 from my recompute of the gate over the shipped option lines; every other shipped line files the served vector, and the roster labels that recompute implies are the pre-check's to serve, not mine. R102: the room was served HOOD 2026-10-16 $120C, the contract open claim r66-run49-HOOD already holds; it is VACATED in both columns - no new leg, and its share line 42.5 sits below the share cut - and the claim's WINDFALL state is not served. EXPIRY AND R4: all ten option legs sit on 2026-10-16 (the only other served date, 2026-10-23, carries WDC and ECHO, both outside the column); AMZN, HPE, SMCI and DELL ship at the full option stake, and NVDA, VST, MU, PLTR, CEG and MRVL ship stamped R4-OVERFLOW (owner, 2026-10-06) at half stake. REQMOVE on the three top legs: AMZN 0.378, HPE 0.302, SMCI 0.469, all inside +3.0%; DELL 3.022 and PLTR 3.29 sit below rank three. MRVL (REQMOVE 6.481) is the leg I would not have chosen; it ships under the owner's ruling. HORIZONS: 3 intraday (BMY, WMT, MSFT), 12 swing (the ten option legs, INTU, GOOGL) and 5 position (CVS, COST, LLY, ABBV, MCK). SHARE COLUMN=CVS 57.0, COST 56.5, LLY 54.5, BMY 54.0, INTU 54.0, WMT 54.0, ABBV 52.5, MSFT 51.5, GOOGL 51.0, MCK 50.0 OPTION COLUMN=AMZN 59.5, HPE 57.0, SMCI 55.5, DELL 53.0, NVDA 51.5, VST 51.5, MU 51.0, PLTR 51.0, CEG 50.0, MRVL 48.0 DIRSORT=[50.0 / 54.0] - the BMY short sits among the longs, so no TAPE-CALL is owed. HOUSE RULES (decided before the scored window, never mid-session): STAKES - shares flat at 1.0 per line (R81); option legs at the full option stake for the first four on 2026-10-16 and half stake, stamped R4-OVERFLOW, for the fifth and later; no adds, no re-entries, no re-strikes. EXITS - every option leg carries its R66 EXIT (ratchet at the contract's break-even, kill close at the house-bracket stop, else close 2026-10-15) and every share line its kill close, fired at the next session's open and never on an intraday print. WINDFALL - a windfall banks half at the first mark the desk serves for that contract (R102) and the rest rides the ratchet; a name with an open claim never ships a second ticket. Desk, R92/R12 - the memo's listings against the persisted book: share: PASS; option: DIFF PRINTED (R92) - AMZN memo 59.5 / shipped 55.0, HPE memo 57.0 / shipped 54.1, SMCI memo 55.5 / shipped 53.6, DELL memo 53.0 / shipped 52.7, NVDA memo 51.5 / shipped 52.2, VST memo 51.5 / shipped 52.2, MU memo 51.0 / shipped 52.0, PLTR memo 51.0 / shipped 52.0, CEG memo 50.0 / shipped 51.7, MRVL memo 48.0 / shipped 51.0

    How this document was produced

    Live board session: FIFTEEN graders - the Decoder on its sheet number 9 - then the Skeptic and the Executive, each a separate model call over the same forty-candidate packet, answering the app's own prompts with each seat's most recent Evening Court lessons prepended. Collector data is real and timestamped. THE PACKET FROZE AT 14:08:06 ET, WITH 111 MINUTES OF TAPE LEFT BEFORE THE CLOSE: every entry is an early-afternoon mark, not an open, and under R14 a window that short makes seat ranks advisory.

On 2026-10-07 my share grades were served sigma in reverse - Spearman(SHARE, stat_signals sigma_daily_pct) -0.994 [n=10], SEAT-COMPUTED: COST 1.14 -> 60 down to INTU 2.84 -> 48 - and my G_OPTIONs were my own break-even sigma-days in reverse, -0.909 [n=10]. Each of my last three lessons took a field away (the direction, the tape, premium as % of spot) and the sheet collapsed onto the one field left. The bare inverse-sigma sort scores -0.624 on that share column; mine scored -0.689 [W=111.9min 14:08:06->16:00:00], LOO [-0.762, -0.613]: I added nothing to the sort but its luck. MRVL, my bottom G_OPTION at 50 as the farthest wing, made +31.71, the column's best. Sigma says how much fragility a line carries - that belongs in the stake and in key_risks, not in the rank; distance in sigmas says what a ticket costs - and in a column of long calls on one expiry a distance sort is a leverage sort, a bet on the sign of the column's one underlying. RULE: no single served field orders a column by itself. CHECK, printed last with the self-check: ONEFIELD=[column: the field my notes cite on the most rows, Spearman(my grades, that field), n], one per column. At |ONEFIELD| >= 0.9 either the sheet prints FACTOR-CALL=<field, the sign I expect it to earn over this W, the served key path that says why this window pays it>, or I re-rank until |ONEFIELD| < 0.9, every row that leaves the field's order naming on the row the second served field that moved it (an event date inside the window, open interest and volume, a served level the name is levered to). Honest size: one court, n=10 and n=8; a factor sort's expected rho over one afternoon is the factor's luck, so this promises no positive rho - it stops me filing a factor bet under the name of fragility, as DIRSORT stopped me filing a direction bet under it.

    Lesson. I JUDGE A REACH WHEN THE BALL STOPS, NOT WHILE IT SPINS. My G_OPTION is a price on reaching break-even before expiry (VIG = break-even % / sigma), so the only evidence that may reorder my option key is the settled-at-exit record: did the underlying close at or past strike + premium by the else-close. One afternoon's premium mark is delta times that afternoon plus time-value drift - on run 51 contract tracked underlying at +0.929 [n=8] [W=111.9min 14:08:06->16:00:00] and 5 of 8 PRICED legs were ILL-CONDITIONED, my top-ranked HPE and DELL the only losers on -0.95% and -0.59% days - so I print that rho, carry it, and never reorder on it. Every G_OPTION row I file carries 'REACH-LEVEL: <strike> + <premium> = <level> by <else-close>' beside its VIG (stated arithmetic, both operands served), so my claim settles from closes alone when no contract mark is served. CHECK: each court prints, for each of my settled legs, REACHED or NOT against my VIG rank (run 51's ten settle by the 2026-10-15 close), and the reach rate of my positive-edge VIG<1 legs beside my VIG>1 legs. Branch, closed now: once ten positive-edge legs have settled, if the VIG<1 reach rate is not above the VIG>1 rate, VIG leaves ORDER for STAKE and signed-E orders the option column; until then the option key stands, labelled 'AT-EXIT n of 10'.

CHECK: the memo's first line reads 'EXPOSURE share s [n] / option o [n]'; any |s| or |o| of 0.50 or more without a TAPE-CALL= line is a failure, and the court scores the falsifier at the close. This promises no rho; it stops me signing a factor bet as a judgment.

    Lesson. I read a call's multiple over open interest against where the strike stood at the prior close, not only against today's price, with a token called MOVED-STRIKE. A notable call's open interest is the prior session's settled figure, struck when that strike sat further from spot. So on a name whose served pct_change_1d in the listed direction is 2.0 or more, a call at 5 DTE or less that BAND reads IN today names no speculator: OWNER none, and the row files 40 to 50 whatever its multiple. A near-spot put on a name already down 2.0 or more on a short reads the same way. The mechanism: when the day's run carries spot onto a strike, yesterday's thin open interest there makes any volume look like a fresh opener. The at-the-money weekly is also the cheapest way to ride a move that has already printed. The footprint therefore restates pct_change_1d instead of adding to it. MOVED-STRIKE reads the open-interest clock of the flow print itself, where CHASE-CAP reads the underlying's own session (my ONE-PRINT lesson). Tonight it moves three of my six speculator rows: CVS 62 (90.0C dte 2 on a 3.52 day), LLY 56 (1220.0C dte 2, 3.43) and HPE 59 (72.0C dte 2, 3.26). Those finished the window at -1.70, -0.71 and -10.32 on the contract. The number that flatters it: with those three at 50, my share rho moves from -0.534 to -0.380 [n=10] and my option rho from -0.108 to -0.037 [n=8] [W=111.9min 14:08:06->16:00:00], both SEAT-COMPUTED. Why it proves nothing: it is fitted on the three rows that suggested it, in one after-the-open session whose prior-close baseline ran -0.729. The share gain is under half the column's SE of 0.378. And it leaves BMY, COST and WMT untouched, which also lost. It earns an out-of-sample test over thirty call- or put-OWNER rows counted in COURTS SAT (R56), not a claim. CHECK: grep tomorrow's notes for MOVED-STRIKE. Every row whose OWNER is a call or put prints 'MOVED-STRIKE day <pct_change_1d> dte <n> TRIPPED|CLEAR', both numbers copied as served literals. Any TRIPPED row above 50 fails outright, one violation enough. The count of rows it tripped prints, so a night it trips none shows as a zero.

    Lesson. No vote without a score. Before I file, I count my non-ABSTAIN lines per column; a column where they would number one or two files every line in that column G_OPTION=ABSTAIN SHARE=ABSTAIN with the lean kept in the stance field, because Spearman needs three lines and anything fewer is a vote the builder reads into the median, the served vector and the fill with no rho to answer for it. REF=median rows count toward the three only in a column that also carries a row I moved off REF on a dated item at HOPS<=2; a REF row never stands alone. The branch is fixed before I read the headlines: per column, moved rows plus same-column REF rows at three or more with at least two distinct grades file; anything less, the whole column is ABSTAIN. This supersedes my 2026-09-29 lesson's REF=median clause wherever it would leave a column at one or two lines. Why: run 51's PLTR G_OPTION=50 REF was my only option line, filed nothing (NON-FILING, R97), and still moved PLTR from the gate's 51.0 to 50.0 in the served vector and the fill's basis (r92_reserve.json; option_fill.json legs[ticker=PLTR].basis_median), which put MU above PLTR in the room's top ten while PLTR's contract beat MU's, +10.89% to +8.07% [W=111.9min 14:08:06->16:00:00]; my two share votes (GOOGL 47, CVS 50 REF) both shipped inside the one-median (n_voting 13 each) under a rho undefined at n=2, and they were ordered backwards (GOOGL +0.70% best, CVS -1.70% worst); my share rho has been undefined at four straight courts sat (47, 48, 49, 51).     Lesson. I HOLD THE TAPE TO THE BAR I HOLD MY WINDOWS TO, AND ASK IT MY OWN QUESTION: CONTINUED BY WHEN? One night's +0.624 (2026-09-25, W=353.8) made today's own-sigma move the thing I order on, while a window class must clear 10 lines and one SE before it authors a point; on 2026-10-07 [W=111.9min 14:08:06->16:00:00] that double standard filed the free signal that failed - my share grades sat +0.954 to the prior-close-to-freeze move, the court's prior_close_baseline read -0.729 [n=10], and my top four (CVS 71, LLY 69, ABBV 67, COST 61) were the column's four worst. IF a line moves off 50 on today's move alone (no TAXON class with authority, no EXHAUSTION CANDIDATE), THEN I type 'TAPE: <today %>/<sigma> = <z> own-sigma UNTESTED [W=<W>]' and the line files inside 47-53, ordered by z, so I still rank (R61) but lend the room's median no conviction the tape has not earned; the tape authors more only once the court's served prior_close_baseline, read by run id from run 51 and split at W=240 minutes, has a mean more than one SE (0.378 at n=10) from zero over three courts sat in that split - and then up to 10 points in that mean's sign, so a fade is licensed that way or not at all. CHECK next court: grep 'TAPE:' - on every tape-only line and no other; my Spearman to the prior-close move beside my rho; the realized return of TAPE lines against the rest within each column, UNDEFINED where a group is empty; the tape record by run id with W. I say three things against it. One: a band that keeps the order buys no rank on a night like this - my -0.767 would stand under it; what it buys is a smaller pull on the one-median (my departure rho -0.620). Two: +0.624 and -0.729 are two nights of opposite sign at two very different W, so the split is a hypothesis I register, not a finding. Three: it is the compression my exhaustion lesson called a deletion, and I accept it only because the tape, unlike that night's order, now has a served record against it and none for it.

I set the number from the levels, the reach and any dated event inside the holding window as if the chain were silent, and the flow stays in the prose and key_risks. CHECK, by someone who does not trust me: the mean share view of the rows whose comment says a print backs the listed direction must sit within one point of the mean share view of the rows whose comment says the chain has no owner for it. Straddles, strangles and parity count in neither group. Tonight that gap is 4.8 points, and any court where it exceeds one point scores the rule FAILED. KILL: it opens at 0 for 0. It is drawn in-sample on one night whose prior-close baseline ran at -0.729, so it may only be the morning's chase wearing a flow label. It is counted in COURTS SAT under R56. If in four of the next five courts sat the rows my comments credit to flow beat the rows they deny on mean direction-signed return, the flow is informative and I delete the rule rather than renaming it.

    Lesson. I will never again let my own stamp be the figure that voids my sheet. R105 clears a number only two ways: it is a literal in my morning prompt, or it is the printed result of + - x / on such literals. A root, a rounding or a percent conversion never clears. On run 51 my REACH ratio, '4.26 / (5.48 x sqrt(7.29)) = 0.288x', was the only failing figure on 34 of my 40 rows, with the CLOCK working chained to it. My own lessons had made that stamp mandatory, and my share order, +0.591 [n=10] as scored [W=111.9min 14:08:06->16:00:00], read undefined [n=1] for me. IF my instrument needs a root, THEN I print its square: 'REACH2 sess=S: BE x BE / (sigma x sigma x S) = q', judged against the squared bar '0.50 x 0.50 = 0.25'. CLOCK v1 stays exactly as written, -round(30 x (ratio - 0.50)) above the bar and 0 at or under it. Its toll is carried only as the gap between my SHARE= and G_OPTION= tokens, so it neither drifts nor prints a figure the test cannot clear, and a court can recompute every toll from the q I print. CHECK: before filing I hold every number on my sheet to R105 myself. Each must be a literal I can point to in my prompt, or the right side of a printed 'a op b = c' whose operands are. The first line of the sheet is a self-audit header that ends 'R105 n/40 CLEAR', and any row short of clear is rewritten before it is filed. KILL: if a court rules that a printed root of a prompt literal clears as stated arithmetic, or the desk serves sqrt(sessions_to_expiry) on each option_contract block, the plain ratio returns the next morning and this check is deleted. I say which in open court.
